desc:
Technical SEO fixes for online stores repair the crawl errors, duplicate pages, redirects and sitemap faults that stop search engines from listing your products. Ecom Swift LLC crawls your store, makes the fixes inside it and sends a before and after list.

## What is technical SEO for an online store?

Technical SEO is the work that makes sure search engines can reach, read and correctly list every page that should appear. It deals with the structure underneath your content: addresses, redirects, canonical tags, sitemaps, the robots file and page status codes.

A store can have excellent products and clear text and still fail here. If a page cannot be crawled or looks like a copy of another page, search engines may leave it out.

## Why technical faults hide in stores

Ecommerce platforms generate pages automatically. A single product can appear under several collection paths. Filters and sort options create new addresses. Old products leave behind pages that error out. Apps and themes add their own redirects and tags, sometimes in conflict.

Owners seldom see any of this, because the store looks normal to a visitor. The faults show up only in a crawl or in the reports inside Search Console.

## How fixing the basics affects traffic and revenue

When search engines waste time on duplicate or broken addresses, the pages that earn money are visited less often and updated more slowly. Repairing the structure points that attention back at real products and collections.

Correct canonical tags tell search engines which version of a page to list. Clean redirects keep old links working. A tidy sitemap shows which pages matter. These changes make your catalog easier to index, but they do not by themselves create demand. Results depend on your competition and content, so we describe the fixes and make no promise about rankings.

## What a technical clean-up covers

- A crawl of your store to find errors and odd status codes.
- Pages that return errors and need a redirect or removal.
- Redirect chains and loops that slow crawlers and visitors.
- Duplicate addresses caused by variants, tags, filters and parameters.
- Canonical tags that point to the wrong page.
- The sitemap, so it lists only pages that should be found.
- The robots file, so it blocks only what it should.
- Search Console errors and coverage messages.
- Internal link structure and orphan pages.
- Mobile checks and hreflang tags for stores that sell in several languages.

## How we fix it

We crawl your store and read your Search Console reports, then sort the findings by risk. We make fixes inside your own store wherever the platform allows, such as redirects, tags, sitemap settings and template changes. Where a platform does not permit a change, we say so and suggest the nearest safe alternative.

The Basic package fixes the most serious crawl and indexing problems, checks the sitemap and robots file and sets up redirects for broken pages. The Standard package widens the crawl, cleans up duplicates, canonical tags and redirect chains and clears Search Console errors where possible. The Premium package adds a structure and internal link review, mobile and hreflang checks and a re-crawl to confirm every fix.

You receive a before and after list. Add-ons include a larger crawl, a log of redirects and an international setup check.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Redirect removed products to the closest relevant page.
- Keep one clear address for each product.
- Check Search Console regularly for new errors.
- Test changes on a few pages before applying them widely.
- Keep your sitemap current as the catalog changes.

**Avoid:**
- Blocking whole sections in the robots file without checking.
- Redirecting every missing page to the home page.
- Stacking redirects on top of redirects.
- Leaving test settings active after a launch.
- Installing several apps that all edit tags and redirects.

## Who this service is for

A store whose pages are missing from search results despite good content will often find the cause here. A seller who has changed theme, apps or addresses over time may carry hidden faults. A shop that sees large numbers of excluded pages in Search Console needs them explained.

It also suits owners preparing for an audit, a redesign or a sale of the business.

## What we need from you

Send your store address and read access to Search Console if you have it. We need collaborator, staff or developer access to make fixes in your store, and we never ask for a password. Tell us about recent changes to the theme or apps. We keep a record of everything we change, so any step can be reversed.
